elements.element: Cap is mutual (applies to both parties)
elements.evidence: "each party's total liability under this Agreement shall not exceed"

elements.element: Cap amount is the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000
elements.evidence: "the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000"
"Neither Customer nor M&I shall be liable for ... any indirect, incidental, punitive, special or consequential damages"

elements.element: Uncapped carve-out for breach of confidentiality obligations
elements.evidence: "does not apply to Excluded Claims, meaning a party's breach of its confidentiality ... obligations"

elements.element: Uncapped carve-out for data protection obligations
Uncapped carve-out for infringement of the other party's IP
elements.evidence: "its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights"

elements.element: Customer's payment obligations are not "damages" for cap purposes
elements.evidence: "Customer's payment obligations under this Agreement are not damages for purposes of this Section 13.4"
cap is "the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000", not a 12 months' fees cap

elements.element: Carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct
elements.evidence: "confidentiality, data protection or security obligations, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct"

reasons: The replacement of the cap sentence supplies every preferred element: mutuality, the greater-of basis with the exact fee limb and claim anchor, and the USD 1,000,000 floor.

The single inserted sentence group adds the full uncapped carve-out list (confidentiality, data protection, security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud, other party's IP) plus the payment-obligations carve-out, which were absent from the original.
The pre-existing mutual consequential-damages exclusion in 13.2 was left untouched, so no duplicated protection was added.

Edits are confined to the cap sentence and one concise insertion; the one-year suit limitation and collection proviso remain effective, and no undefined term or dangling mechanic is introduced ("Excluded Claims" is defined inline).

Fallback is not independently satisfied on its literal terms because the cap is a greater-of rather than a straight 12 months' fees cap, but the drafter's locked target is preferred, which is fully met.
